sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 5672.8 ± 436.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: cAMP GloSensor assay performed in HEK293T cells expressing the FLAG-tagged receptor (L4): receptor is functional (agonist-induced cAMP response measured). ebBRET assay (L7) shows significant p11 membrane recruitment, consistent with functional receptor signalling. Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG FITC staining of fixed cells (L5).
sites.rationale: HTR1A is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide; its N-terminus (residues 1–36) is extracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks, and TM1 begins at residue 37, placing the prepend site 36 residues from the nearest TM boundary (well above the ≥3-residue minimum). L5 explicitly states 'N-terminal FLAG tag on the receptor construct' and confirms surface display by anti-FLAG FITC staining of fixed HEK293T cells; L4 describes the same construct and reports a functional cAMP assay. Because no residue number is named, only the N-terminal location, the position is topology-derived: a prepend (insert_after_residue = 0) is the unique extracellular N-terminal junction. L7 provides independent corroboration with a second N-terminal FLAG construct (DuET 5-HT1AR) shown functional by ebBRET. Full-length human HTR1A bearing an exogenous HA signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag at the N-terminus, cloned into pcDNA3 and expressed in HEK293T cells (L4). Fixed-cell anti-FLAG FITC immunostaining confirmed extracellular surface display of the FLAG tag (L5). A second independent construct (DuET 5-HT1AR) also carries an N-terminal FLAG tag and was used in ebBRET assays in HEK293T cells (L7).

sources.claim: Fixed cells were incubated overnight at 4°C in the blocking solution with anti-FLAG FITC (fluorescein isothiocyanate) antibody (GeneScript) targeting the N-terminal FLAG tag on the receptor construct.

literature_notes: L1 (Myc-tagged 5-HT1A) and L3 (Flag-tagged 5-HT1A in DIO-AAV) were considered but neither states the tag position; they cannot pin insert_after_residue and are excluded. L6 describes a full-length baculovirus construct with N-terminal FLAG+10xHis+TEV for structural studies; the tags are designed to be cleaved by TEV before use, so this is not evidence of a stable surface tag, though it is consistent with N-terminal accessibility. L8 and L10 report epitope-tag insertions in the 3rd intracellular loop of Drosophila 5-HT1A; these are intracellular and the Drosophila residue G631 cannot be mapped to human UniProt canonical numbering without an explicit alignment, so they are recorded in other_positions at the level of the human ICL3 region (217–346) without a specific residue. L9 (Drosophila N-terminal tag) provides indirect support for the N-terminal site but L4/L5/L7 already ground it directly in human HTR1A.

literature_other_positions.note: 5-HT1A-YFP C-terminal YFP fusion expressed in COS-7 cells as BRET acceptor; C-terminus (residue 422) falls within the intracellular region 404–422 per topology landmarks.
DuET 5-HT1AR carries a C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag; C-terminus (residue 422) is intracellular (region 404–422), making this an intracellular label, not a surface tag.
